name: std::clamp

declarations.code:
template <class T>

constexpr const T &clamp(const T &v, const T &lo, const T &hi);

intro:
If the value of v is within [lo, hi], returns v; otherwise returns the nearest boundary.

1) Uses operator<(until C++20)std::less{}(since C++20) to compare the values.

If T is not LessThanComparable, the behavior is undefined.[1]

2) Uses the comparison function comp to compare the values.

If lo is greater than hi, the behavior is undefined.

↑ If NaN is avoided, T can be a floating-point type.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
v

 -

 the value to clamp


 lo, hi

 -

 the boundaries to clamp v to


 comp

 -

 comparison function object (i.e. an object that satisfies the requirements of Compare) which returns true if the first argument is less than the second.

The signature of the comparison function should be equivalent to the following:
bool cmp(const Type1& a, const Type2& b);
While the signature does not need to have const&, the function must not modify the objects passed to it and must be able to accept all values of type (possibly const) Type1 and Type2 regardless of value category (thus, Type1& is not allowed, nor is Type1 unless for Type1 a move is equivalent to a copy(since C++11)).

The types Type1 and Type2 must be such that an object of type T can be implicitly converted to both of them.

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: Reference to lo if v is less than lo, reference to hi if hi is less than v, otherwise reference to v.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.text:
1) At most two comparisons using operator<(until C++20)std::less{}(since C++20).

2) At most two applications of the comparison function comp.

sections.title: Possible implementation
Notes
sections.text:
std::clamp

int n = -1;
const int& r = std::clamp(n, 0, 255); // r is dangling

If v compares equivalent to either bound, returns a reference to v, not the bound.

guides.name: std::clamp
guides.summary: Keep a value inside a chosen range.
guides.analogy: Like a volume control that cannot go below 0 or above 100, even when you ask it to.
guides.signature:
template<class T>
const T& clamp(const T& value, const T& low, const T& high);
guides.note: The lower bound must not exceed the upper bound. Copy the result when passing temporary values; keeping the returned reference can dangle.
